d.t: The act of corroding or consuming some substance.
Food.
d.e: When are we going to get some eats?

d.t: Water.
The underside of a roof that extends beyond the external walls of a building.
d.e: Him that you term'd Sir, the good old Lord Gonzallo, / His teares runs downe his beard like winters drops / From eaues of reeds: […]

d.t: Something that extends over or projects beyond.
d.e: But after many strains and heaves / He got up to the Saddle eaves.

d.t: To hear (intentionally) a conversation one is not intended to hear; to listen in.
d.e: I hope nobody was eavesdropping on our conversation last night, since it got so personal.

d.t: To listen for another organism's calls, so as to exploit them.
d.e: […] Eastern Red Bat will eavesdrop on the sonar calls of other red bats to locate potential insect prey.

d.t: The dripping of rain from the eaves of a house.
The space around a house on which such water drips.
A concealed aperture through which an occupant of a building can surreptitiously listen to people talking at an entrance to the building.
The act of intentionally hearing a conversation not intended to be heard.
d.e: Were you having a little eavesdrop on us last night?

d.t: One who eavesdrops.
A surveillance aircraft.
d.e: […] the Japanese Ministry of Defence rang the bell and informed the world's press about the Tokyo Express — the ironic Japanese nickname for the constant flow of Soviet flying eavesdroppers in Japanese airspace.

d.t: verbal noun of eavesdrop:
